Anita: Heads-up — saw a perf regression on the reranker/embeddings endpoint after the recent kernel selector change. Quick dump of numbers from yesterday's canary:
perf-bot: perf/run/emb-rerank-compact-v2 — median latency 28ms -> 42ms, p95 120ms -> 210ms, tokens/sec drop ~28%. Link: https://pprof.internal/2046122222/flare
Anita: Config snippet we used on canary:
```
batcher: { policy: compact_batch, target_token_budget: 2048, prefill_ms: 8, priority_sampler: recency_weighted }
kernel_selector: auto_pref_bf16
```
Chao: Thanks. Is KV cache being hit for these requests? rerank/emb are usually single-turn so shouldn't use KV much. If KV thrash, that'll inflate latency for sure.
Marta: I pulled a flamegraph — most time is in small-gemm path and kernel fallback layer. Looks like selector picked quantized kernel which then falls back into slower path for odd sequence dims. pprof shows a spike in memcpy and kernel-compat checks.
Jared: Reproduced locally with microbench. When target_token_budget is low we end up with many tiny batches and more kernel switches. Increasing token budget changed batch shape and reduced kernel switches.
Anita: Interesting. Hypothesis: compact_batch policy + low token budget creates many sub-32 token microbatches which triggers a different kernel path (non-vectorized). Also our kernel selector currently prefers BF16 when available but doesn't account for sequence-length/distribution for non-chat workloads.
Chao: For rerank endpoints the sequence length is tiny (16-64). Maybe we should bias selector toward small-gemm-optimized kernels for non-chat models. Also consider a fallback that prefers fewer kernel switches per GPU: pin kernel affinity per worker for X minutes.
Marta: Agreed. Proposed quick experiments:
- A: bump target_token_budget=4096 for rerank traffic and run canary 50%
- B: add kernel_affinity: true for compact_batch workers (sticky kernel for 60s)
- C: adjust sampler to prefer aggregating requests up to N=8 before emission (max_latency 30ms)
Which order makes sense?
Jared: I'd do C then A. Aggregation reduces churn immediately. Then A to change economics of batch formation. B is slightly more intrusive (sticky kernel might hide regressions) but we should try it in staging.
Anita: I'll open a quick PR to change sampler to aggregation-first for non-chat rerank endpoints and add a canary flag. Also adding a new metric: kernel_switches_per_sec and batch_shape_histogram.
Chao: For testing, run: `./tools/run_micro --model rerank-compact-v2 --concurrency 256 --tokens 32 --policy compact_batch --measure kernel_switches` and compare with baseline.
perf-bot: Canary started (canary-id=canary-2147) — 10% traffic to dedicated-pool-emb-rerank. Will post results in 10m.
Marta: Also note KV cache contribution: even single-turn re-rank path touches KV routines when we do prefill for dense rerank scoring. We should verify prefill_ms=8 isn't causing duplicate KV builds under high concurrency.
Jared: Quick note — quantized kernels sometimes go through codepath that allocates small temp buffers per request; those allocations are expensive under high batch counts. Aggregation reduces alloc churn.
Anita: Action items: (1) PR for aggregation-first sampler (owner: Anita), (2) canary bump target_token_budget to 4096 (owner: Chao), (3) experiment kernel_affinity sticky flag in staging (owner: Marta), (4) add kernel_switches_per_sec metric and batch_shape_histogram dashboard (owner: Jared).
Anita: I'll also attach my local flamegraph and the microbench command in the PR. Thanks :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy queued: pr/emb-rerank-agg-sampler -> staging (ETA ~3m).
Chao: If canary shows latency improvement we should consider making compact_batch default for rerank non-chat; otherwise revert quickly. Keep an eye on cost delta.
Marta: Will follow up with p95/p99 dashboards and the kernel_switches metric. If we still see high memcpy we might need to tweak kernel selector heuristics (match on seq_len distribution + batch_size).
Anita: Great — I'll update thread when staging canary finishes.
